title: Golden Salmon Cakes with Lemon Mayo
subtitle: crisp pan-fried salmon cakes from pantry cans, with a bright lemon-garlic mayo and buttered rice and peas
imageAlt: Golden salmon cakes with a dollop of lemon mayo and a lemon wedge beside rice and peas on a white plate with a navy napkin
servingsNote: 8 cakes: dinner for one big eater + one hungry eater, plus 2 lunches

beforeYouStart.text: Canned salmon has soft, edible bones and skin; mash them in for calcium or pick them out, your choice.
Start the rice first. The cakes firm up best with 15 minutes in the fridge.

steps.title: Start the rice
steps.text: Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear. Bring it to a boil with the water and a pinch of salt, cover and simmer on low 15 minutes, then rest 10 minutes off the heat with the lid on. Fluff with a fork.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Zest and juice the lemon. Flake the salmon into a bowl and mix with the panko, eggs, 2 tbsp mayonnaise, 1 tsp of the lemon zest, garlic powder, onion powder, salt and pepper.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Shape into 8 cakes about 2 cm thick and chill 15 minutes on a plate.

steps.title: Lemon mayo
steps.text: Stir the ⅓ cup mayonnaise, 1 tbsp lemon juice and garlic powder together.

steps.title: Fry
steps.text: Heat the oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium. Cook the cakes 4 minutes a side, until deep golden and 74°C (165°F) in the centre.

steps.title: Peas
steps.text: Microwave the peas, covered, with a splash of water 3–4 minutes; stir them into the rice with the butter.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Two cakes per plate with the rice and peas and a spoon of lemon mayo.

fixIt.fix: Chill them longer, and don't flip until the first side is deep golden; add 2 tbsp more panko if the mix is wet.
Drain the salmon less well, or add another tablespoon of mayonnaise to the mix.
The heat was too high. Medium, not medium-high, and check with a thermometer.

saleTip: Canned pink salmon is the budget pick at No Frills; sockeye is redder and richer if it's on sale.
swap: Air fryer: brush the cakes with oil and cook at 200°C, 10–12 minutes, flipping halfway, to 74°C (165°F).
leftovers: Cold salmon cakes make a great sandwich with the lemon mayo.
doneness: 74°C (165°F) in the centre because of the raw egg (Health Canada, egg dishes), above the 70°C (158°F) for fish; the salmon is already cooked in the can.
source: Based on tested canned salmon cake methods (Canadian Living, Clover Leaf test kitchen): drained canned salmon bound with egg, crumbs and mayonnaise, chilled, then pan-fried over medium.
prepAhead: Shape the cakes up to 1 day ahead; keep covered in the fridge.
Freeze shaped raw cakes on a tray, then bag; cook from thawed.
reheat: At 200°C (400°F) for 10 minutes, or the air fryer at 190°C for 6 minutes, until 74°C (165°F).

basic.note: Salmon cakes with plain mayonnaise; no lemon or onion powder.

stepNotes.1: Basic: skip the lemon zest and onion powder.

fancy.note: Crisp quick-pickled cucumber on the side.

addSteps.title: Quick cucumber
addSteps.text: Toss the cucumber with the rice vinegar, sugar and a pinch of salt and let it sit 15 minutes while the cakes chill.

plating: Two cakes overlapping on the rice.
Lemon mayo on top, a lemon wedge beside.

why.0-0: Canned salmon is already cooked, cheap and keeps for years in the pantry.
why.0-1: Panko binds without making the cakes heavy.
why.0-2: Eggs hold the cakes together as they fry.

funFact: Most canned salmon sold in Canada is wild Pacific salmon from British Columbia and Alaska.

keeps.note: freeze cooked or raw shaped cakes
